key_concepts: Rocks can be described by texture, color, grain size, hardness, and toughness
Texture is whether a rock surface feels smooth or rough
Grain size is the size of particles in a rock and affects its texture
Hardness is resistance to deformation and scratching; toughness is resistance to fracturin
Igneous rocks form from crystallization of magma or lava inside or outside a volcano
Sedimentary rocks form under the ocean by burial and compaction of sediments
Metamorphic rocks form deep underground by deformation and metamorphism of other rocks
Igneous rocks are usually the hardest and contain shiny crystals
Sedimentary rocks are usually the softest, have layers, may contain fossils, and have weak
Metamorphic rocks are usually harder than sedimentary rocks and have thin layers
Rocks can be classified as igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic using observable features
